The Astros were attempting to become the fourth consecutive wild card team to win the Series , following the Anaheim Angels ( 2002 ) , Florida Marlins ( 2003 ) and Boston Red Sox ( 2004 ) . Both teams were attempting to overcome decades of disappointment , with a combined 132 years between the two teams without a title . The Astros were making their first Series appearance in 44 years of play , while the White Sox had waited exactly twice as long for a title , having last won the Series in 1917 , and had not been in the Series since 1959 , three years before the Astros ' inaugural season . Like the 1982 World Series between the St. Louis Cardinals and the Milwaukee Brewers , the 2005 World Series is one of only two World Series in the modern era ( 1903 -- present ) with no possibility for a rematch between the two opponents , because the Astros moved to the American League in 2013 . Pen and ink drawings often use hatching -- groups of parallel lines . Cross-hatching uses hatching in two or more different directions to create a darker tone . Broken hatching , or lines with intermittent breaks , form lighter tones -- and controlling the density of the breaks achieves a gradation of tone . Stippling uses dots to produce tone , texture and shade . Different textures can be achieved depending on the method used to build tone . Drawings in dry media often use similar techniques , though pencils and drawing sticks can achieve continuous variations in tone . Typically a drawing is filled in based on which hand the artist favors . A right - handed artist draws from left to right to avoid smearing the image . Erasers can remove unwanted lines , lighten tones , and clean up stray marks . In a sketch or outline drawing , lines drawn often follow the contour of the subject , creating depth by looking like shadows cast from a light in the artist 's position . Sometimes the artist leaves a section of the image untouched while filling in the remainder .

Reading were promoted to English football 's top division for the first time in their history . The 2006 -- 07 season saw Reading make their first appearance in the top flight of English football . Reading defied pre-season predictions of relegation to finish the season in eighth place with 55 points . Reading turned down the chance to play in the UEFA Intertoto Cup . In the run up to their second season in the Premier League , Reading took part in the 2007 Peace Cup in South Korea . This second season was less successful , however , and Reading were relegated back to the Championship . Reading started the 2008 -- 09 season with a 15 match unbeaten home run . They finished fourth and qualify for the play - offs , where they lost to Burnley in the semi-final . Manager Steve Coppell resigned just hours after the game , replaced by Brendan Rodgers . Rodgers left the club by mutual consent on 16 December 2009 and Brian McDermott made caretaker manager the same day .

facts.0.116: Faced with losing her position at Witches 5, Eudial creates a computer program to find the true owners of the three Talismans.
facts.0.117: Eudial learns that Haruka and Michiru are the ones who hold two of the Talismans within their own hearts.
facts.0.118: Eudial and her companions take away Usagi's brooch, and follow Eudial onto a lonely island.
facts.0.119: The invitation turns out to be a trick, and Michiru's pure heart is taken, which turns into the mystical Deep Aqua Mirror.
facts.0.120: Haruka, in order to release her own talisman, shoots herself with Eudial's gun.
facts.0.121: Haruka's pure heart transforms into the mystical Space Sword.
facts.0.122: Episode 111 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'The Purity Chalice', the Viz Media title 'The Holy Grail's Mystical Power: Moon's Double Transformation', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Seihai no shinpi na chikara! Mūn nidan henshin'.
facts.0.123: Episode 111 was directed by Hiroki Shibata, written by Sukehiro Tomita, art directed by Kazuyuki Hashimoto, and animation directed by Ikuko Itō. It originally aired on October 22, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 11, 2000.
facts.0.124: Sailor Pluto appears and reawakens Sailors Uranus and Neptune.
facts.0.125: The three talismans resonate with each other, the third and last being Sailor Pluto's Garnet Orb.
facts.0.126: The Holy Grail appears, and Sailor Moon grabs it and evolves into Super Sailor Moon.
facts.0.127: Super Sailor Moon drives Eudial out.
facts.0.128: Mimete kills Eudial by sabotaging her car with snails.
facts.0.129: Episode 112 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Show Stoppers', the Viz Media title 'Who is the True Messiah? Chaos of Light and Darkness', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Shin no kyūseishu wa dare? Hikari to kage no kaosu'.
facts.0.130: Episode 112 was directed by Noriyo Sasaki, written by Shigeru Yanagawa, art directed by Minoru Ōkōchi, and animation directed by Shinya Hasegawa. It originally aired on November 5, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 12, 2000.
facts.0.131: The girls end up watching the filming of a movie, where Chibiusa encounters Hotaru, whom she quickly befriends.
facts.0.132: In the end, Chibiusa is revealed to be the 12-year-old daughter of Professor Souichi Tomoe, the possessed leader of the Death Busters.
facts.0.133: Super Sailor Moon uses her new 'Rainbow Moon Heartache' attack to defeat the Daimon of the day.
facts.0.134: Episode 113 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Rini's Risky Friendship', the Viz Media title 'A House Filled With Evil Presence: The Beautiful Hotaru's Secret', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Yōki tadayou ie! Bishōjo Hotaru no himitsu'.
facts.0.135: Episode 113 was directed by Kōnosuke Uda, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on November 12, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 13, 2000.
facts.0.136: The three Outer Guardians appear to Tuxedo Mask, and tell him why they cannot fight alongside Sailor Moon and the other four Sailor Guardians.
facts.0.137: Usagi and Chibiusa visit Hotaru, and see a woman who looks like Kaolinite.
facts.0.138: The Messiah of Silence appears demanding pure hearts.
facts.0.139: Episode 114 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Mimet's Mess', the Viz Media title 'I Love Idols: Mimete's Dilemma', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Aidoru daisuki! Nayameru Mimetto'.
facts.0.140: Episode 114 was directed by Harume Kosaka, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Yoshiyuki Shikano, and animation directed by Masahiro Andō. It originally aired on November 19, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 14, 2000.
facts.0.141: Minako and Mimete enter a beauty contest at the same time, with Mimete willing to risk it all to obtain victory.
facts.0.142: Both Minako and Mimete fall short of the needed votes to win the idol position.
facts.0.143: Mimete decides to go back to her evil ways.
facts.0.144: Episode 115 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'The Shadow of Silence', the Viz Media title 'Shadow of Silence: The Pale Glimmer of a Firefly', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Chinmoku no kage!? Awaki Hotaru hi no yurameki'.
facts.0.145: Episode 115 was directed by Takuya Igarashi, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Katsumi Tamegai. It originally aired on November 26, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 17, 2000.
facts.0.146: Hotaru overexerts herself and is hospitalized, during which her past without friends is shown, and the reasons for it.
facts.0.147: Meanwhile, Mimete targets a soap opera actor.
facts.0.148: During the attack on the actor, the attacking Daimon runs near Hotaru, who glows and completely freezes the Daimon.
facts.0.149: Episode 116 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Thorny Weather', the Viz Media title 'Sunny Skies After a Storm: A Friendship Dedicated to Hotaru', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Arashi nochi hare! Hotaru ni sasageru yūjō'.
facts.0.150: Episode 116 was directed by Yūji Endō, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Jouji Yanase. It originally aired on December 3, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 18, 2000.
facts.0.151: Mamoru takes Usagi, Chibiusa and Hotaru to a botanical garden that is tended by Yoshiki Kurebayashi, an old classmate of Mamoru's.
facts.0.152: While there, Mimete targets Yoshiki's pure heart and causes a storm that puts the plants at risk.
facts.0.153: Sailor Moon defeats the accompanying Daimon, U-Bara.
facts.0.154: Episode 117 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Heightened Hazard', the Viz Media title 'Higher and Stronger: A Cheer from Usagi', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Yori takaku yori tsuyoku! Usagi no ōen'.
facts.0.155: Episode 117 was directed by Kunihiko Ikuhara, written by Shigeru Yanagawa, art directed by Minoru Ōkōchi, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on December 10, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 19, 2000.
facts.0.156: Hotaru wishes to give a letter to Shun Hayase, a famous athlete.
facts.0.157: Shun Hayase becomes targeted when Hotaru goes to give the letter to him.
facts.0.158: Hotaru possessively blasts the enemy with a hugely strong amount of energy.
facts.0.159: Hotaru talks to Shun about being frail and weak, and he thanks her for talking to him.
facts.0.160: Episode 118 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'It's In The Cards', the Viz Media title 'The Battle Inside the Demonic Space: The Sailor Guardians' Gamble', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Makū no tatakai! Sērā Senshi no kake'.
facts.0.161: Episode 118 was directed by Noriyo Sasaki, written by Katsuyuki Sumisawa, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Masahide Yanagisawa. It originally aired on December 17, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on July 20, 2000.
facts.0.162: Mimete attempts to create a Daimon by herself, throwing the entire Tomoe house into another dimension.
facts.0.163: The Guardians enter the dimension and are defeated by a game-master Daimon named U-Ikasaman.
facts.0.164: Hotaru manages to assist in U-Ikasaman's defeat by the use of a bluff.
facts.0.165: Episode 119 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Goodness Eclipsed', the Viz Media title 'The Messiah of Silence Awakens? Stars of Destiny', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Chinmoku no Meshia kakusei? Unmei no hoshiboshi'.
facts.0.166: Episode 119 was directed by Harume Kosaka, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Shinya Hasegawa. It originally aired on December 24, 1994 and aired in English in the United States on September 13, 2000.
facts.0.167: The Sailor Guardians visit a planetarium, where a man is attacked by a Daimon.
facts.0.168: The symbol of Saturn appears on Hotaru's forehead, and she attacks the Daimon.
facts.0.169: Sailor Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto attack Hotaru, since she is both Sailor Saturn, the Sailor Guardian of Silence, Ruin and Birth, and also possessed by the Messiah of Silence.
facts.0.170: Super Sailor Moon takes the blow to protect Hotaru.
facts.0.171: Episode 120 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Next In Line', the Viz Media title 'An Invasion from an Another Dimension: Mystery of Infinity Academy', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Ijigen kara no shinryaku! Mugen Gakuen no nazo'.
facts.0.172: Episode 120 was directed by Kōnosuke Uda, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Minoru Ōkōchi, and animation directed by Katsumi Tamegai. It originally aired on January 7, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 21, 2000.
facts.0.173: Chibiusa goes to Hotaru's house to find that Hotaru has disappeared, and is devastated about it.
facts.0.174: At the same time, the Sailor Guardians investigate Infinity Academy.
facts.0.175: Mimete tries one final time to defeat the Sailor Guardians before Tellu literally pulls the plug on her operation.
facts.0.176: Episode 121 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Fiendish Ferns', the Viz Media title 'A Bewitching Flower That Steals Hearts: Tellu, the Third Witch', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Kokoro wo ubau yōka! Daisan no majō Teruru'.
facts.0.177: Episode 121 was directed by Takuya Igarashi, written by Shigeru Yanagawa, art directed by Kazuyuki Hashimoto, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on January 14, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 24, 2000.
facts.0.178: Tellu develops a new plan to steal pure hearts, using a plant bred for that purpose.
facts.0.179: Setsuna realizes the plant is an alien plant made to steal pure hearts, and warns the Sailor Guardians.
facts.0.180: Tuxedo Mask causes a mutated plant to destroy Tellu.
facts.0.181: This leads the Sailor Guardians to trace Tellu back to the mysterious Infinity Academy.
facts.0.182: Episode 122 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'The Science Of Love', the Viz Media title 'Believe in Love: Ami, the Kindhearted Guardian', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Ai wo shinjite! Ami, kokoro yasashiki Senshi'.
facts.0.183: Episode 122 was directed by Yūji Endō, written by Sukehiro Tomita, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Hideyuki Motohashi. It originally aired on January 21, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 25, 2000.
facts.0.184: Ami investigates the Infinity Academy, where she meets Viluy, the fourth of the Witches 5.
facts.0.185: Viluy attempts to use her nanorobots to steal pure hearts from entrance exam takers.
facts.0.186: After Viluy's battle, her own microscopic robots turn against her, destroying her in the process.
facts.0.187: Episode 123 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Wake Up Call', the Viz Media title 'Shadows of Destruction: the Messiah of Silence Awakens', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Hametsu no kage! Chinmoku no Meshia no mezame'.
facts.0.188: Episode 123 was directed by Harume Kosaka, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Minoru Ōkōchi, and animation directed by Mari Tominaga. It originally aired on January 28, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 26, 2000.
facts.0.189: Cyprine is the last of the Witches 5.
facts.0.190: Cyprine steals pure hearts from Infinity Academy students.
facts.0.191: The Sailor Guardians engage Cyprine, and her alter-ego, Ptilol, in a showdown.
facts.0.192: Chibiusa is abducted by the recently resurrected Kaolinite.
facts.0.193: Chibiusa's pure heart is stolen by Mistress 9, who has taken over Hotaru's body, which allows her to awaken as the Messiah of Silence.
facts.0.194: Episode 124 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Who's Really Who?', the Viz Media title 'The Coming Terror of Darkness: Struggle of the Eight Guardians', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Semari kuru yami no kyōfu! Kusen no Hassenshi'.
facts.0.195: Episode 124 was directed by Takuya Igarashi, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kazuyuki Hashimoto, and animation directed by Ikuko Itō. It originally aired on February 4, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 28, 2000.
facts.0.196: Mistress 9 uses all remaining Daimon eggs to create a powerful energized shield of evil minions around Infinity Academy.
facts.0.197: Sailor Moon is abducted, as she is the holder of the Holy Grail.
facts.0.198: After witnessing Sailor Pluto ultimately sacrificing herself to save them by using her forbidden ability to stop time, Sailor Uranus and Sailor Neptune destroy Germatoid.
facts.0.199: Germatoid is the Daimon possessing Professor Souichi Tomoe.
facts.0.200: Sailor Uranus and Sailor Neptune destroy Germatoid with their talismans, the Deep Aqua Mirror and the Space Sword.
facts.0.201: Episode 125 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Darkness, My Old Friend', the Viz Media title 'The Shining Shooting Star: Saturn and the Messiah', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Kagayaku ryūsei! Satān soshite kyūseishu'.
facts.0.202: Episode 125 was directed by Kōnosuke Uda, written by Yoji Enokido, art directed by Kenichi Tajiri, and animation directed by Ikuko Itō. It originally aired on February 11, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 29, 2000.
facts.0.203: Sailor Moon is tricked into giving Mistress 9 the Holy Grail, which she uses to summon Pharaoh 90 to Earth.
facts.0.204: Hotaru regains consciousness with the assistance of Sailor Moon and her father, destroying Mistress 9.
facts.0.205: Hotaru fully awakens the spirit of Sailor Saturn within herself at last.
facts.0.206: Sailor Saturn returns Chibiusa's pure heart crystal.
facts.0.207: Sailor Saturn appears before Sailor Moon to ultimately sacrifice herself and destroy Pharaoh 90 once and for all with her destructive powers.
facts.0.208: Sailor Moon gains the help of the other six Sailor Guardians to become Super Sailor Moon once more.
facts.0.209: Super Sailor Moon saves both Hotaru and Sailor Saturn.
facts.0.210: Sailor Saturn is reborn as a baby immediately afterward.
facts.0.211: Episode 126 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Second Chance', the Viz Media title 'A New Life: Parting of the Stars of Destiny', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Atarashiki seimei! Unmei no hoshiboshi betsuri no toki'.
facts.0.212: Episode 126 was directed by Yūji Endō, written by Megumi Sugihara, art directed by Kazuhisa Asai, and animation directed by Taichi Nakamura. It originally aired on February 18, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on July 30, 2000.
facts.0.213: Haruka and Michiru give the newly reborn infant Hotaru to a still-healing Professor Souichi Tomoe, who is finally free of the Death Busters.
facts.0.214: Haruka and Michiru viciously attack Sailor Moon, for she protected Hotaru's body and Sailor Saturn, and risked the whole entire world for one mere life.
facts.0.215: The Silver Crystal throws Haruka and Michiru back.
facts.0.216: Haruka and Michiru kneel to Sailor Moon as their leader and leave the city.
facts.0.217: Episode 127 has the Cloverway Inc. title 'Tough Kindness', the Viz Media title 'A Guardian's Realization: Strength Lies Within a Pure Heart', and the original Japanese title romanized as 'Senshi no Jikaku! Tsuyosa wa Pyua na Kokoro no Naka ni'.
facts.0.218: Episode 127 was directed by Harume Kosaka and written by Sukehiro Tomita. It originally aired on February 25, 1995 and aired in English in the United States on August 1, 2000.
facts.0.219: Chibiusa returns to the future after receiving a letter from her mother, Neo-Queen Serenity.
facts.0.220: Meanwhile, a final Daimon emerges from the rubble of Infinity Academy.
facts.0.221: Chibiusa returns just in time to help defeat the final Daimon.

Type Sociedad Anónima Industry Retail Founded Arteixo , Galicia ( 24 May 1974 ; 43 years ago ( 1974 - 05 - 24 ) ) Founder Amancio Ortega Headquarters Arteixo , Galicia Number of locations 2266 stores Area served Worldwide Products Clothing Revenue US $ 15.9 billion ( 2016 ) Parent Inditex Website zara.com Zara ( Spanish : ( ˈθaɾa ) ) is a Galician fast fashion ( clothing and accessories ) retailer based in Arteixo , Galicia . The company was founded in 1975 by Amancio Ortega and Rosalía Mera . It is the main brand of the Inditex group , the world 's largest apparel retailer . The fashion group also owns brands such as Massimo Dutti , Pull&Bear , Bershka , Stradivarius , Oysho , Zara Home , and Uterqüe .

Zara (retailer)
Products ( edit ) Zara stores have men 's and women 's clothing , as well as children 's clothing ( Zara Kids ) . Zara 's products are supplied based on consumer trends . Its highly responsive supply chain ships new products to stores twice a week . After products are designed , they take ten to fifteen days to reach the stores . All of the clothing is processed through the distribution center in Spain . New items are inspected , sorted , tagged , and loaded into trucks . In most cases , the clothing is delivered within 48 hours . Zara produces over 450 million items per year . Reportedly , Zara needs just one week to develop a new product and get it to stores , compared to the six - month industry average , and launches around 12,000 new designs each year .

During the 1980s , Ortega changed the design , manufacturing , and distribution process to reduce lead times and react to new trends in a quicker way , which he called `` instant fashions '' . The improvements included the use of information technologies and using groups of designers instead of individuals . Zara 's previous logo Expansion ( edit ) In 1988 , the company started its international expansion through Porto , Portugal . In 1989 , it entered the United States , and then France in 1990 . During the 1990s , Zara expanded to Mexico ( 1992 ) , Greece , Belgium and Sweden ( 1993 ) . In the early 2000s , Zara opened its first stores in Japan and Singapore ( 2002 ) , Russia and Malaysia ( 2003 ) , China , Morocco , Estonia , Hungary and Romania ( 2004 ) , the Philippines , Costa Rica and Indonesia ( 2005 ) , South Korea ( 2008 ) , India ( 2010 ) , and South Africa and Australia ( 2011 ) .

On September 2010 , Zara launched its online boutique . The website began in Spain , the UK , Portugal , Italy , Germany and France . In November that same year , Zara Online extended the service to five more countries : Austria , Ireland , the Netherlands , Belgium and Luxembourg . Online stores began operating in the United States in 2011 , Russia and Canada in 2013 , and Mexico , Romania , and South Korea in 2014 . . India In 4 october 2017 . Zara introduced the use of RFID technology in its stores in 2014 . The RFID chips are located in the security tags which are removed from clothing when it is purchased and can be reused . The chip allows the company to quickly take inventory by detecting radio signals from the RFID tags . When an item is sold , the stockroom is immediately notified so that the item can be replaced . An item that is not on the shelf can easily be found with the RFID tag . In 2015 , Zara was ranked 30 on Interbrand 's list of best global brands .
